paragraphs: When the Feast of Pentecost arrived, they were all together in one place. Out of nowhere came a sound like a strong wind at gale force — nobody could tell where it was coming from. It filled the entire building. Then, like wildfire, the Holy Spirit swept through the whole group, and they started speaking in all kinds of different languages, exactly as the Spirit gave them the words.

There were a lot of Jews staying in Jerusalem at the time — devout pilgrims from all over the world. When they heard the sound, they came running. Then, one by one, they heard their own mother tongues being spoken, and it blew their minds. They couldn't figure out what was happening and kept saying, "Wait — aren't these guys all Galileans? How are we hearing them speak our own languages? Parthians, Medes, and Elamites; visitors from Mesopotamia, Judea, and Cappadocia; Pontus and Asia, Phrygia and Pamphylia; Egypt and the parts of Libya near Cyrene; immigrants from Rome, both Jews and proselytes; even Cretans and Arabs — they're speaking our languages, telling about God's mighty works!"
Their heads were spinning — they couldn't make sense of any of it. They kept asking each other, totally confused: "What is going on here?"
Others just joked, "They're drunk on cheap wine."

That's when Peter stood up — backed by the other eleven — and spoke out, bold and urgent: "Fellow Jews, all of you visiting Jerusalem, listen carefully and get this story straight. These people aren't drunk, whatever some of you think. They haven't even had time to get drunk — it's only nine in the morning! This is what the prophet Joel said would happen: 'In the Last Days,' God says, 'I will pour out my Spirit on every kind of people: your sons will prophesy, and so will your daughters; your young men will see visions, your old men will dream dreams. When the time comes, I'll pour out my Spirit on those who serve me — men and women both — and they'll prophesy. I'll set wonders in the sky above and signs on the earth below — blood and fire and billowing smoke, the sun turning black and the moon blood-red — before the Day of the Lord arrives, the Day tremendous and marvelous. And whoever calls out to me, God, for help will be saved.'"

"Fellow Israelites, listen carefully to these words. Jesus the Nazarene was a man fully accredited by God to you — the miracles, wonders, and signs God did through him are common knowledge. This Jesus, following God's deliberate and well-thought-out plan, was betrayed by men who took the law into their own hands and handed over to you. And you nailed him to a cross and killed him. But God untied the ropes of death and raised him up — death was no match for him. David said it all: 'I saw God before me for all time. Nothing can shake me; he's right by my side. I'm glad from the inside out, ecstatic; I've pitched my tent in the land of hope. I know you'll never dump me in Hades; I'll never even smell the stench of death. You've got my feet on the life-path, with your face shining sun-joy all around.'"

"Dear friends, let me be completely frank with you. Our ancestor David is dead and buried — his tomb is right there in plain sight today. But David was also a prophet, and he knew God had solemnly sworn that one of his descendants would rule his kingdom. Seeing far into the future, he spoke about the resurrection of the Messiah — 'no trip to Hades, no stench of death.' This Jesus is the one God raised up, and every one of us here is a witness to it. Then, lifted up to the highest place at God's right hand, he received the promised Holy Spirit from the Father and poured out the Spirit he had just received. What you see and hear right now is that outpouring. David himself never ascended to heaven, but he did say: God said to my Master, 'Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool to rest your feet on.' So all Israel, know this for certain: there is no more room for doubt — God has made him both Master and Messiah, this Jesus whom you killed on a cross."
Cut to the heart, the listeners asked Peter and the other apostles, "Brothers! Brothers! What do we do now?"

Peter said, "Change your life. Turn to God and be baptized, each one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ, so your sins will be forgiven. Receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. This promise is for you and your children — and also for all who are far away, in fact for everyone our Master God invites."
He kept going like this for a long time, urging them again and again: "Get out while you can — get out of this sick and twisted generation!"
That day about three thousand took him at his word — they were baptized and signed up. They committed themselves to the apostles' teaching, to life together, to the shared meals, and to prayer.

Everyone around was in awe at all the wonders and signs being done through the apostles. All the believers lived in wonderful harmony, holding everything in common. They sold what they owned and pooled the money so that everyone's needs were met.

Every day they worshiped together in the Temple, then shared meals at home — every meal a celebration, exuberant and joyful — as they praised God. People in general liked what they saw. And every day their number kept growing, as God added those who were being saved.
title: The Holy Spirit Drops In
